Another glaring example of how the state weaponizes national security laws to lock people away without trial has just been checked by the judiciary. The Punjab and Haryana High Court has rightly granted regular bail to an accused booked under provisions relating to national security and the Official Secrets Act, explicitly holding that "mere suspicion of sharing sensitive information with a person in Pakistan cannot justify prolonged incarceration." 

For too long, marginalized individuals have borne the brunt of these draconian, fear-mongering laws that prioritize state paranoia over basic human rights and due process. The state loves to throw around terrifying buzzwords—in this case, claiming the individual was allegedly in telephonic contact with Karachi-based “Punjabi Kuri”—to justify locking people up indefinitely and trampling on their liberty. 

This systemic overreach destroys lives while hiding behind the shield of national security. While this court order offering his release is a welcome intervention against indefinite detention, it lays bare the urgent need for deep institutional reform to dismantle these oppressive legal mechanisms once and for all.

Look, what we are seeing here is yet another undeniable proof of how the ruling establishment weaponizes heavy-handed national security laws to crush human rights and lock people away without trial. The Punjab and Haryana High Court has rightly stepped in to grant regular bail to an accused booked under provisions relating to national security and the Official Secrets Act. The court explicitly held that "mere suspicion of sharing sensitive information with a person in Pakistan cannot justify prolonged incarceration." 

For too long, marginalized individuals have borne the brunt of these draconian, fear-mongering laws that prioritize state paranoia over basic human rights and due process. The state loves to throw around terrifying buzzwords—in this case, claiming the individual was allegedly in telephonic contact with Karachi-based “Punjabi Kuri”—to justify locking people up indefinitely and trampling on their liberty. 

This systemic overreach destroys lives while hiding behind the shield of national security. While this court order offering his release is a welcome intervention against indefinite detention, it lays bare the urgent need for deep institutional reform to dismantle these oppressive legal mechanisms once and for all.

source_text:
Look, what we are seeing here is yet another undeniable proof of how the ruling establishment weaponizes heavy-handed national security laws to crush human rights and lock people away without trial. The Punjab and Haryana High Court has rightly stepped in to grant regular bail to an accused booked under provisions relating to national security and the Official Secrets Act. The court explicitly held that "mere suspicion of sharing sensitive information with a person in Pakistan cannot justify prolonged incarceration." 

For too long, marginalized individuals have borne the brunt of these draconian, fear-mongering laws that prioritize state paranoia over basic human rights and due process. The state loves to throw around terrifying buzzwords—in this case, claiming the individual was allegedly in telephonic contact with Karachi-based “Punjabi Kuri”—to justify locking people up indefinitely and trampling on their liberty. 

This systemic overreach destroys lives while hiding behind the shield of national security. While this court order offering his release is a welcome intervention against indefinite detention, it lays bare the urgent need for deep institutional reform to dismantle these oppressive legal mechanisms once and for all.

This is the kind of weak-kneed institutional failure that puts our borders and our nation at risk. While the liberal commentariat whines about state paranoia and demands the dismantling of our legal mechanisms in the name of human rights, they completely ignore personal responsibility and the sacred duty of protecting the homeland. We need strong borders, firm authority, and unwavering defense of our country—not coddling suspects who jeopardize our safety.
